## Natural history notes

A small freshwater shrimp characterized by its nearly transparent body, long antennae, and slender legs. In Florida, it is found in ponds, lakes, marshes, swamps, ditches, and slow-moving streams with aquatic vegetation or submerged cover. It feeds on algae, detritus, and small organic particles, serving as an important food source for fish, wading birds, and other aquatic predators.
